title: Grade 8 Math — Thu, May 21
description: Rational Numbers — Day 4 of 5: Properties and comparison
subject: mathematics

questions.question: Which is greater: −3/5 or −2/3?
questions.explanation: Convert to common denominator 15: −3/5=−9/15, −2/3=−10/15. −9/15 > −10/15 (less negative). So −3/5 > −2/3.

questions.question: If a/b is a rational number and a/b > 0, then:
options: a and b are both positive OR both negative
a is positive and b is negative
a is negative and b is positive
questions.explanation: Positive rational: same signs numerator and denominator (both + or both −). 3/4 = positive. (−3)/(−4) = positive.

questions.question: The rational number 0 has how many reciprocals?
questions.explanation: 0 has NO multiplicative inverse (reciprocal). 0 = 0/1 → reciprocal would be 1/0 = undefined.

questions.question: Which statement is TRUE?
options: Every rational number is an integer
Every integer is a rational number
Every rational number is a natural number
questions.explanation: Every integer n = n/1 → rational. But not every rational is an integer (e.g., 1/2 is not an integer).

questions.question: Absolute value |−7/8| = ?
questions.explanation: Absolute value = distance from 0 = always positive. |−7/8| = 7/8.

questions.question: For which values of x is x/4 a negative rational number?
questions.explanation: x/4 < 0 when x < 0 (negative numerator, positive denominator = negative).

questions.question: Is the commutative property valid for subtraction of rational numbers?
questions.explanation: Subtraction is NOT commutative. 3/4 − 1/2 = 1/4, but 1/2 − 3/4 = −1/4. They differ.

questions.question: Property: p/q + (−p/q) = 0. This shows:
options: Every rational number has an additive inverse
questions.explanation: p/q + (−p/q) = 0 demonstrates that every rational has an additive inverse (opposite). −p/q is the additive inverse of p/q.

questions.question: Using the number line: which is greater, −1/4 or −3/4?
questions.explanation: On the number line, −1/4 is to the right of −3/4. Right = greater. −1/4 > −3/4.

questions.question: Complete: rational numbers form a ___ under all four operations (excluding division by 0).
options: Closed system (field) — all four operations produce a rational
Closed only under addition and subtraction
Set where only multiplication is closed
questions.explanation: Rational numbers are closed under +, −, ×, and ÷ (except ÷0). This completeness makes them a mathematical field.
